reasoning: The claim is fully supported by comprehensive scientific data. Continuous satellite monitoring of Arctic sea ice began in 1979. Data from major scientific organizations—including NASA, NOAA, the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC), and the European Environment Agency—confirm a highly significant, long-term downward trend in both Arctic sea ice extent and thickness. This decline is apparent in all seasons but is most pronounced during the annual late-summer minimum in September, which has decreased by over 12% per decade relative to the 1981–2010 average.
